verdict.rationale: Source availability under an open license is a fair question for a note-taking app, so the axis applies, but nothing in the evidence shows Obsidian's own application source is published under an open license. The items that come closest don't qualify: the public obsidian-api repo and sample-plugin tutorials are developer building blocks for plugins, 'free without limits' is pricing rather than licensing, and plain-text Markdown storage concerns data openness, not code openness.
